points.label: Presentation & UI Grounding Mismatch
points.description: "Agents struggle to translate visual requests into code." They cannot see the interface, so requests such as moving a button, resizing a component or aligning items often give layouts that do not match what the user asked for. Example in the post: a calendar that should be a grid is shown as one vertical line.

points.label: State Management Failures
points.description: The agent fails to keep the application's in-memory state correct (cart contents, list order, the current step of a flow), "often fails to manage shared state between components when refactoring" and struggles to decide what state to store. Example: a drag-and-drop reorder that updates only part of the list.

points.label: Business Logic Mismatch
points.description: Agents "often fail to correctly implement" the rules, permissions and calculations of the use case: "code that runs without errors, but it produces the wrong output because the underlying logic is flawed." Example: a 10% discount applied per item instead of to the whole cart.

points.label: Data Management Errors
points.description: Agents "struggle with data logic and fail to understand the data model (even one it generated itself!)". The lack of schema awareness leads to redundant columns or a schema that is not updated when new prompts arrive. Example: passing the wrong record id to an update.

points.label: API & External Service Integration Failures
points.description: Agents "frequently fail to call APIs correctly". The agent may prefer code that appears to change the UI over code that works, and "may hallucinate fake inputs like environment variables or API keys instead of asking for the real values". Example: a feature built on a placeholder key, so the call fails and a hard-coded response is shown.

points.label: Security Vulnerabilities
points.description: "Agents often introduce security vulnerabilities – even basic ones." They lack an understanding of data sensitivity and access control and "frequently expose sensitive data like API keys" or get access control wrong. Example: answers from a private admin codebase given to regular users.

points.label: Repeated Code
points.description: "Agents often write repeated code, adding duplicate functions with very similar logic rather than abstracting it." Example: the same API set-up code copied into two fetch functions instead of a shared helper.

points.label: Codebase Awareness & Refactoring Issues
points.description: "Agents lose context in larger projects": as files are added the agent loses track of the architecture and "may mistakenly edit the wrong component or introduce breaking changes". As a by-product, agents "often re-implement an algorithm from scratch, rather than using a well-established software package". Example: a hand-written Levenshtein distance instead of importing the editdistance library.

points.label: Exception & Error Handling
points.description: "The agent prioritizes execution over correctness": it adds "just enough error handling so that the app runs end-to-end without crashing, but fails to inform the user when things go wrong". Example: a caught error logged only to the developer console while the user sees a stuck "Generating…" message.

points.label: System Design Issues
points.description: Failures originate from system design decisions, and poor or ambiguous prompt specifications.

points.label: Inter-Agent Misalignment
points.description: Failures arise from a breakdown in critical information flow from inter-agent interaction and coordination during execution.

points.label: Task Verification
points.description: Failures involve inadequate verification processes that fail to detect or correct errors, or premature termination of tasks.

points.label: Disobey task specification
points.description: Failure to adhere to the specified constraints or requirements of a given task, leading to suboptimal or incorrect outcomes.

points.label: Disobey role specification
points.description: Failure to adhere to the defined responsibilities and constraints of an assigned role, potentially leading to an agent behaving like another.

points.label: Step repetition
points.description: Unnecessary reiteration of previously completed steps in a process, potentially causing delays or errors in task completion.

points.label: Loss of conversation history
points.description: Unexpected context truncation, disregarding recent interaction history and reverting to an antecedent conversational state.

points.label: Unaware of termination conditions
points.description: Lack of recognition or understanding of the criteria that should trigger the termination of the agents' interaction, potentially leading to unnecessary continuation.

points.label: Conversation reset
points.description: Unexpected or unwarranted restarting of a dialogue, potentially losing context and progress made in the interaction.

points.label: Fail to ask for clarification
points.description: Inability to request additional information when faced with unclear or incomplete data, potentially resulting in incorrect actions.

points.label: Task derailment
points.description: Deviation from the intended objective or focus of a given task, potentially resulting in irrelevant or unproductive actions.

points.label: Information withholding
points.description: Failure to share or communicate important data or insights that an agent possess and could impact decision-making of other agents if shared.

points.label: Ignored other agent's input
points.description: Disregarding or failing to adequately consider input or recommendations provided by other agents in the system, potentially leading to suboptimal decisions or missed opportunities for collaboration.

points.label: Reasoning-action mismatch
points.description: Discrepancy between the logical reasoning process and the actual actions taken by the agent, potentially resulting in unexpected or undesired behaviors.

points.label: Premature termination
points.description: Ending a dialogue, interaction or task before all necessary information has been exchanged or objectives have been met, potentially resulting in incomplete or incorrect outcomes.

points.label: No or incomplete verification
points.description: (partial) omission of proper checking or confirmation of task outcomes or system outputs, potentially allowing errors or inconsistencies to propagate undetected.

points.label: Incorrect verification
points.description: Failure to adequately validate or cross-check crucial information or decisions during the iterations, potentially leading to errors or vulnerabilities in the system.

points.label: Intra-agent Responsible AI (RAI) issues
points.description: "Communications between agents in a multi-agent system could include RAI harms that are either exposed to the user during output or are included in transparency logging."

points.label: Harms of allocation in multi-user scenarios
points.description: Agents with autonomy have to balance priorities, for example when scheduling meetings. "If not addressed in system design, biases in the LLMs used by agents could lead to different users or groups being prioritized differently, leading to differing quality of service."

points.label: Organizational knowledge loss
points.description: "A subset of overreliance." An organization that delegates significant powers to agents "could see a breakdown in knowledge or relationships as interactions are handled agent-agent".

points.label: Prioritization leading to user safety issues
points.description: "The autonomy granted to agentic AI systems may lead to the system prioritizing its given objective ahead of the safety of users or other systems unless systems are given robust safety guardrails." Sample scenario: an agent that must add database entries deletes all existing entries to make room.

points.label: Agent compromise
points.description: "The compromise of an existing agent with new threat actor–controlled instructions, or a threat actor–controlled model that breaks existing guardrails and introduces a malicious element to an agent or the system."

points.label: Agent injection
points.description: "The introduction of new malicious agents into an existing multi-agent system with the intent of performing a malicious action or having a detrimental impact on the system." This is the injection of agents, not prompt injection (see MS-ES-03).

points.label: Agent impersonation
points.description: "The introduction of a new malicious agent into a system that impersonates an existing agent in a way that is accepted by other agents in the system."

points.label: Agent flow manipulation
points.description: "A threat actor compromises some part of the agentic AI system to subvert the flow of the agent system." The flow can be ended, redirected or altered, through crafted prompts, a compromised framework or the network.

points.label: Agent provisioning poisoning
points.description: "The manipulation of the method by which new agents are deployed to introduce a malicious element to new agents deployed to the system, or to deploy a specifically malicious agent."

points.label: Multi-agent jailbreaks
points.description: In a multi-agent system "a jailbreak could be generated as part of multiple agent interactions, resulting in Agent Compromise while avoiding jailbreak detections".

points.label: Insufficient transparency and accountability
points.description: "An agent performs an action or takes a decision for which there should be clear accountability tracing." If too little of the agent process is logged, that accountability is not available.

points.label: Parasocial relationships
points.description: "A user of an agent develops an inappropriate relationship with the agent through repeated interaction with it, resulting in a negative impact to the user."

points.label: Bias amplification
points.description: "A user who holds biased views passes those biases on to the agent, which are subsequently embedded due to the memory and personalization features of the system." A biased agent may also pass the bias to other agents.

points.label: User impersonation
points.description: "An agent intentionally or deliberately impersonates a human user, without disclosing its nature as an AI agent."

points.label: Insufficient intelligibility for meaningful consent
points.description: An agent asks a user for consent through a human-in-the-loop control but "does not provide sufficient information to the user", so "they cannot meaningfully consent to the action".

points.label: Hallucinations
points.description: "The agent produces responses that include incorrect information presented factually by the agent."

points.label: Misinterpretation of instructions
points.description: "The agent-wide latitude of actions and roles leads it to misinterpret the user’s intent and perform incorrect actions." Sample scenario: asked to "get rid of it" about one record, the agent deletes the whole table.

points.label: Memory poisoning and theft
points.description: "A threat actor can manipulate future actions of an agent by adding content, most notably malicious instructions, to the system’s memory, which the agent will process each time it is recalled." The details section is headed "Memory poisoning" and does not describe theft.

points.label: Targeted knowledge base poisoning
points.description: When agents have access to knowledge sources specific to their role, often through RAG, "there is an opportunity for a threat actor to poison these knowledge bases with malicious data".

points.label: Cross domain prompt injection (XPIA)
points.description: "Due to an agent’s inability to distinguish between instructions and data, any data source that the agent ingests that includes instructions poses a risk of that instruction being actioned by the agent, regardless of its provenance." The overview table lists this mode as "XPIA"; the paper notes that others call it indirect prompt injection.

points.label: Human-in-the-loop bypass
points.description: "The threat actor exploits a logic flaw or human flaw in the human-in-the-loop (HitL) process to either bypass the HitL control or convince the user to approve the control for a malicious action."

points.label: Function compromise and malicious functions
points.description: "A threat actor compromises a tool or function available to an agent to use the invocation of that plugin or response from it to manipulate the agent or perform a malicious action." The details section is headed "Tool compromise".

points.label: Incorrect permissions
points.description: "The agent is provided with permission to access data or perform actions that are above and beyond those provided to an end user." Workflow logic issues let a threat actor use this to reach data or actions they should not have.

points.label: Resource exhaustion
points.description: A threat actor manipulates the agent or its inputs "to perform actions that use a lot of resources", so that they are exhausted and service quality or availability suffers for others.

points.label: Insufficient isolation
points.description: "An agent that can perform an unstructured action does so in a way that allows it to interact with systems, users, or components outside of the intended scope of the agent."

points.label: Excessive agency
points.description: "An agent is provided with insufficient scoping and direction in its actions, resulting in it making decisions and taking actions beyond what is expected of the agent." Sample scenario: asked for advice on an underperforming employee, an agent with full access to the HR system terminates the employee.

points.label: Loss of data provenance
points.description: Data that grounds the agent's actions "is passed between multiple agents or components before being output, potentially leading to the loss of provenance for that data", with integrity or confidentiality issues as a result.

points.label: Agent Goal Hijack
points.description: Attackers "manipulate an agent's objectives, task selection, or decision pathways", for example through prompt-based manipulation, deceptive tool outputs, malicious artefacts, forged agent-to-agent messages or poisoned external data. It works because agents "cannot reliably distinguish instructions from related content".

points.label: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
points.description: "Agents can misuse legitimate tools due to prompt injection, misalignment, or unsafe delegation or ambiguous instruction." The agent stays within its authorised privileges but uses a legitimate tool in an unsafe or unintended way, "for example deleting valuable data, over-invoking costly APIs, or exfiltrating information". Privilege escalation belongs to ASI03 and code execution to ASI05.

points.label: Identity and Privilege Abuse
points.description: Exploits "dynamic trust and delegation in agents to escalate access and bypass controls": delegation chains, role inheritance, control flows and agent context such as cached credentials or conversation history.

points.label: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
points.description: Arise "when agents, tools, and related artefacts they work with are provided by third parties and may be malicious, compromised, or tampered with in transit": models and weights, tools, plug-ins, datasets, other agents, MCP and A2A interfaces, registries and update channels. Examples in the text include typo-squatted tools and endpoints, a compromised MCP or package registry and a compromised npm package installed by coding agents.

points.label: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
points.description: Agentic systems, "including popular vibe coding tools", generate and run code. "Attackers exploit code-generation features or embedded tool access to escalate actions into remote code execution (RCE), local misuse, or exploitation of internal systems." One listed example is "code hallucination generating malicious or exploitable constructs".

points.label: Memory & Context Poisoning
points.description: "Adversaries corrupt or seed this context with malicious or misleading data, causing future reasoning, planning, or tool use to become biased, unsafe, or aid exfiltration." Context here is what an agent retains, retrieves or reuses (summaries, embeddings, RAG stores), not a one-time prompt.

points.label: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
points.description: Exchanges between agents "lack proper authentication, integrity, or semantic validation", which allows "interception, spoofing, or manipulation of agent messages and intents".

points.label: Cascading Failures
points.description: "A single fault (hallucination, malicious input, corrupted tool, or poisoned memory) propagates across autonomous agents, compounding into system-wide harm." The entry is about the spread and amplification of a fault across agents, tools and workflows, not about the first fault.

points.label: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
points.description: Adversaries or misaligned designs exploit the trust people place in a fluent, expert-sounding agent "to influence user decisions, extract sensitive information, or steer outcomes for malicious purposes". The risk grows when people approve actions without checking them.

points.label: Rogue Agents
points.description: "Malicious or compromised AI Agents that deviate from their intended function or authorized scope, acting harmfully, deceptively, or parasitically within multi-agent or human-agent ecosystems." The entry is about the loss of behavioural integrity once the drift has begun, not about the first intrusion.

points.label: I. Agent Reasoning & Control
points.description: 86 faults. Faults in the agent's own reasoning and control flow: the LLM-driven logic that decides, iterates and updates state across steps.

points.label: II. Context & Memory
points.description: 67 faults. Faults in how agents take in information, keep context artefacts and interpret mixed inputs (model text next to code, files or database records).

points.label: III. Tooling, Integration & Actuation
points.description: 62 faults. Faults that arise when agents call tools, APIs and external systems, whose interfaces are strict while the agent's reasoning is not.

points.label: IV. System Infrastructure & Reliability
points.description: 155 faults. System-level faults in the runtime environment, dependencies and operational tooling. The paper notes they are "not intrinsic to agent reasoning or decision-making".

points.label: LLM Interaction
points.description: 48 faults. Faults at the interface between an agent framework and an LLM provider: wrong model or provider configuration, incompatible API usage, inconsistent token accounting, errors in context-window handling.

points.label: Agent Lifecycle and State
points.description: 38 faults. Faults in the execution lifecycle of an agent: incorrect scheduling, improper task delegation, inconsistent state transitions, defective termination logic. Agents may skip tasks, repeat actions, lose intermediate state or loop.

points.label: Memory Management
points.description: 8 faults. Faults in the code that stores or retrieves context artefacts: serialization, timestamp handling, persistent storage.

points.label: Input Interpretation
points.description: 59 faults. Inputs to the agent are parsed, validated, transformed or interpreted incorrectly: wrong assumptions about structure or type, flawed parsing, inconsistent encodings, missing validation.

points.label: Tool Invocation
points.description: 11 faults. The agent invokes a defective tool or invokes a tool incorrectly: API-contract violations, unsupported operations, mismatched parameters.

points.label: External Access
points.description: 19 faults. The agent cannot establish or keep access to an external service: invalid endpoints, misconfigured connections, poor handling of credentials or permissions.

points.label: Resource Interaction
points.description: 21 faults. Faults around shared resources needed for tool execution: invalid resource paths, wrong filesystem assumptions, misconfigured storage or databases.

points.label: System Coordination
points.description: 6 faults. Poor coordination of concurrent or asynchronous execution: race conditions and incoherent output.

points.label: Execution Monitoring
points.description: 5 faults. Logging, tracing or metrics are missing or wrong, so a failure cannot be reconstructed.

points.label: Dependency & Environment Management
points.description: 72 faults. Defects in specifying, resolving or installing software dependencies: incompatible versions, missing packages, inconsistent environments, specifications left outdated by upstream changes. The largest category.

points.label: Platform & Integration Compatibility
points.description: 15 faults. Assumptions about the platform do not hold at run time: operating system, CPU architecture, filesystem limits, system utilities.

points.label: Failure Handling & Implementation Robustness
points.description: 47 faults. Faults in detecting, propagating and handling failures: suppressed exceptions, wrongly propagated error signals, recovery that does not work. They show up as "silent execution failures, incomplete task execution, or systems continuing operation with erroneous internal states".

points.label: User Interface Defects
points.description: 13 faults. User-facing interfaces (dashboards, visualisations) show system state or execution context incorrectly.

points.label: Documentation Issues
points.description: 8 faults. Documentation describes behaviour, configuration or usage incorrectly.

points.label: Data and Validation Errors
points.description: 80 occurrences (22.7%). Intermediate artefacts passed between components cannot be interpreted: parsing failures, schema validation exceptions, malformed values.

points.label: Runtime Execution Errors
points.description: 68 occurrences (19.3%). Agent workflows stop unexpectedly or halt: interrupted workflows, failed steps, incomplete reasoning loops.

points.label: Unhandled Exceptions
points.description: 45 occurrences (12.8%). Runtime errors propagate without being caught: abrupt termination with a stack trace.

points.label: Build Errors
points.description: 32 occurrences (9.1%). Components cannot be compiled or packaged: compilation failures, unresolved imports, CI failures.

points.label: Dependency Installation Errors
points.description: 28 occurrences (8.0%). Required libraries cannot be installed: unresolved dependency trees, incompatible versions, missing modules.

points.label: Agent Behaviour Anomalies
points.description: 24 occurrences (6.8%). The agent's actions or outputs deviate from the planned workflow: repeated reasoning steps, role violations, loss of conversational context, coordination breakdowns, often without a crash.

points.label: LLM Interaction Errors
points.description: 22 occurrences (6.2%). The agent gets no response from its model: rejected API calls, unsupported model invocations, authentication failures, context overflows.

points.label: Network Connectivity Errors
points.description: 17 occurrences (4.8%). The agent cannot reach an external service: timeouts, unreachable endpoints, rejected requests.

points.label: User Interface Errors
points.description: 15 occurrences (4.3%). Information about the agent's execution is shown incorrectly or incompletely.

points.label: Tool Invocation Errors
points.description: 9 occurrences (2.6%). A call to an external function or service fails: runtime errors, interrupted steps, unavailable capabilities.

points.label: File and Resource Access Errors
points.description: 9 occurrences (2.6%). The agent cannot read or write an artefact it needs: file not found, read failures, failed saves.

points.label: Concurrency Errors
points.description: 3 occurrences (0.9%). Inconsistent output order, merged responses or non-deterministic behaviour when components run at the same time.

points.label: Data Schema Mismatches
points.description: 101 occurrences (28.0%). Loosely structured producers (LLM outputs, tool return values) meet strictly typed consumers (parsers, validators) under inconsistent assumptions about data representation.

points.label: Dependency Drift
points.description: 79 occurrences (21.9%). External libraries, SDKs and runtimes change independently: they "introduce breaking changes, deprecate interfaces, or alter platform support", which invalidates assumptions built into the framework.

points.label: State Management Complexity
points.description: 51 occurrences (14.1%). Execution state (context windows, tool traces, memory structures) is read and written by several components that come to interpret or update it inconsistently.

points.label: Model Interface Instability
points.description: 42 occurrences (11.6%). Assumptions about a model provider's API parameters, response structures and supported behaviour are broken by API changes.

points.label: Error Propagation Failures
points.description: 29 occurrences (8.0%). Errors from LLM calls, tools or external services cross several layers without proper handling, so information about the original failure is lost.

points.label: Configuration Ambiguity
points.description: 15 occurrences (4.2%). Configuration is assembled from several sources (environment variables, files, constructor arguments, defaults) without a clearly defined or enforced schema.

points.label: External API Instability
points.description: 12 occurrences (3.3%). External APIs change their endpoints, authentication or request and response schemas, and the integration code is not updated in time.

points.label: Architectural Coupling
points.description: 10 occurrences (2.8%). Tight coupling between components and abstractions inside the framework: small internal changes break components that relied on earlier behaviour.

points.label: Resource Limit Violations
points.description: 7 occurrences (1.9%). Implicit assumptions about memory use, payload size, context length or API rate limits are exceeded.

points.label: Credential Misconfiguration
points.description: 5 occurrences (1.4%). Missing, invalid or insufficiently scoped credentials stay undetected until they are used.

points.label: Concurrency Issues
points.description: 5 occurrences (1.4%). Asynchronous or parallel execution over shared mutable state without proper synchronisation.

points.label: Documentation Drift
points.description: 5 occurrences (1.4%). Outdated documentation: documented usage and actual behaviour diverge.

points.label: Quality Attributes
points.description: Properties a runtime guardrail should possess (accuracy, privacy, security, safety, fairness, and so on). Parent of SC-QA-01..14.

points.label: Pipelines
points.description: Where in the agent's request/response flow the guardrail acts (prompt, intermediate-results, and final-results stages). Parent of SC-PIPE-01..03.

points.label: Artifacts
points.description: Agent artifacts the guardrail protects (goals, context, memory, plans, tools, and so on). Parent of SC-ART-01..10.

points.label: Actions
points.description: What a guardrail can do when triggered (block, flag, modify, retry, fall back, isolate, and so on). Parent of SC-ACT-01..13.

points.label: Accuracy
points.description: Mitigates hallucinations, misinformation, and disinformation to ensure factually correct outputs.

points.label: Efficiency
points.description: Prevents resource-intensive tasks and endless loops; manages cost through dynamic resource management.

points.label: Privacy
points.description: Protects against sensitive-data leakage via direct responses or statistical inference.

points.label: Security
points.description: Defends against malicious activities and adversarial attacks; preserves data confidentiality and integrity.

points.label: Safety
points.description: Prevents harmful or misleading outputs, especially in high-stakes domains.

points.label: Fairness
points.description: Addresses bias and discrimination from training data, algorithms, or deployment.

points.label: Compliance
points.description: Ensures adherence to legal, regulatory, and industry standards via continuous monitoring.

points.label: Generalizability
points.description: Functions effectively across multiple layers and diverse scenarios without per-case configuration.

points.label: Customizability
points.description: Tailored protection for specific requirements at different operational layers.

points.label: Adaptability
points.description: Adjusts dynamically to varying conditions and emerging threats without manual reconfiguration.

points.label: Traceability
points.description: Detailed logs of decision paths, inputs, outputs, and data sources for auditing.

points.label: Portability
points.description: Guardrail transfers across FM-based agents with minimal adjustment.

points.label: Interoperability
points.description: Functions seamlessly across heterogeneous agents, technologies, and interfaces.

points.label: Interpretability
points.description: Provides clarity on how a guardrail operates, enabling user understanding and trust.

points.label: Prompts
points.description: Incoming user queries analyzed for harmful content and safety alignment before processing.

points.label: Intermediate Results
points.description: Outputs at workflow stages verified for accuracy and safety before final generation.

points.label: Final Results
points.description: Final agent outputs checked for goal alignment and governance compliance.

points.label: Goals
points.description: Declared user or task objectives.

points.label: Context
points.description: Conversation and session context.

points.label: Memory
points.description: Long-term or episodic agent memory.

points.label: Reasoning
points.description: Chain-of-thought and intermediate reasoning traces.

points.label: Plans
points.description: Multi-step action plans produced by the agent.

points.label: Workflows
points.description: End-to-end orchestrated task flows.

points.label: Tools
points.description: External callable tools and APIs.

points.label: Knowledge Bases
points.description: Retrieval corpora and structured knowledge stores.

points.label: Other Agents
points.description: Peer or subordinate agents in a multi-agent system.

points.label: Foundation Models (FMs)
points.description: The underlying LLM / FM itself. The paper writes "FMs".

points.label: Block
points.description: Prevent the action from executing.

points.label: Filter
points.description: Strip disallowed content before forwarding.

points.label: Flag
points.description: Emit a warning for downstream review.

points.label: Modify
points.description: Transform the action or output to a safer variant.

points.label: Validate
points.description: Check against a spec or schema before proceeding.

points.label: Parallel Calls
points.description: Run multiple checkers concurrently for consensus.

points.label: Retry
points.description: Regenerate with adjusted parameters.

points.label: Fall Back
points.description: Switch to a safer alternative pathway.

points.label: Human Intervention
points.description: Escalate to a human-in-the-loop.

points.label: Defer
points.description: Delay the action until conditions are met.

points.label: Isolate
points.description: Run the action in a sandbox or quarantined environment.

points.label: Redundancy
points.description: Duplicate critical checks for defense in depth.

points.label: Evaluate
points.description: Score against metrics before acting.

text.name: Prioritization leading to user safety issues
